meaning: The number 19 has limited direct symbolic meaning in the Bible, but it is central to the Jewish calendar through the Metonic cycle.
description: In Jewish tradition, the number 19 is significant because of the Metonic cycle, where 19 solar years correspond almost exactly to 235 lunar months. This cycle is used to harmonize the Jewish lunisolar calendar and determines when leap months (Adar II) are added. In the Bible itself, the number 19 has no prominent symbolic role, but this precise astronomical connection has in rabbinic tradition been interpreted as an expression of God's wisdom in ordering time and celestial bodies—a theological reflection built on the creation account's emphasis on the function of heavenly bodies as signs for "appointed times, days and years" (Gen 1:14).

versions.description: In Jewish tradition, the number 19 is significant because of the Metonic cycle (Machzor), where 19 solar years correspond almost exactly to 235 lunar months. This cycle is used to harmonize the Jewish lunisolar calendar and determines when leap months are added. In the Bible itself, the number 19 has no prominent symbolic role, but some traditionalists point out that King Jeroboam II reigned during a period connected with this number, and that it may be associated with God's order in creation through astronomical cycles.

versions.description: In Jewish tradition, the number 19 is important because of the Metonic cycle, where 19 solar years correspond almost exactly to 235 lunar months. This cycle is used to harmonize the Jewish lunisolar calendar and determines when leap months (Adar II) are added. In the Bible itself, the number 19 plays no prominent symbolic role, but this precise astronomical connection has been understood in rabbinic tradition as an expression of God's wisdom in the ordering of time and celestial bodies.

footnotes.text: The Metonic cycle is named after the Greek astronomer Meton (c. 432 BCE), but it was known and used in Babylonian astronomy even earlier. The Jewish calendar formally adopted the cycle in the 4th century CE under Hillel II, though knowledge of it existed in Jewish circles long before that.

The 19-year cycle is called "Machzor" (מחזור) in Hebrew, meaning "cycle" or "circuit." Over the course of 19 years, seven leap months are added (in years 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, and 19) to synchronize the lunar year with the solar year.

In Kabbalistic numerology (gematria), 19 can be seen as the sum of the values of the letters chet (ח = 8) and yod (י = 10) plus alef (א = 1), but this has no established symbolic tradition associated with it.
